_about: Community layouts: shared roots used by save-redirection layers.
These are DIRECTORIES, which are filesystem facts. Nothing here identifies or
attributes whoever produced a layer, and NOVARA has no business doing so; the only
question is where a user's saves are so they can be backed up.
match_kind 'any' because a shared root is a convention of the layer, not a fact
about one game, so ONE entry covers every game that layer wraps.
CRITICAL: each is keyed INSIDE the path by {TITLE} or {STEAM_APPID}. A shared
multi-game root keyed only by {WILDCARD} would fan out across every subfolder, and
every game would then claim every other game's saves.
TOOL-AGNOSTIC BY DESIGN. Where a layer inserts its own name between the shared root
and the per-game folder, that segment is a {WILDCARD} rather than a literal. One rule
then covers every tool using that shape -- including tools that do not exist yet --
and the corpus never becomes a list of named tools. The {STEAM_APPID} leaf is what
keeps it game-specific.
PAIRED ENTRIES. Several layers keep the actual save payload in a 'remote' subfolder
alongside metadata files. Both are listed: the precise 'remote' path at a lower
priority number so it wins when present, and the parent as a fallback that still
captures everything if the layout differs. Same pattern as the Rockstar entries.
VERIFIED against a real machine during Track G. Corrections made as a result are
noted per entry -- two earlier guesses were wrong about both the anchor and the leaf,
which is exactly why entries carry provenance.
